Deltona officials say parade is getting cancelled due to the state’s voter-approved Amendment 3 property tax overhaul

A city in southwestern Florida has cancelled its Christmas parade, citing pending state legislation, to ensure the city remains “fiscally responsible”.

City officials in Deltona said the parade – which typically include floats, marching bands, dancers and Santa Claus appearing in the finale – was getting cancelled due to Florida’s voter-approved property tax overhaul.
